habitat.naturalHabitat: Respiratory epithelium of humans and other hosts, with avian and swine reservoirs
habitat.hostAssociation: Infects humans, birds (natural reservoir), and pigs; capable of zoonotic spillover and genetic reassortment
habitat.environmentalOccurrence: Can survive briefly on surfaces and in respiratory droplets; wild aquatic birds are the primary natural reservoir
habitat.reservoir: Wild aquatic birds as the natural reservoir; also pigs and humans

microscopy.appearance: Electron microscopy in research settings shows pleomorphic enveloped particles studded with hemagglutinin (HA) and neuraminidase (NA) surface glycoproteins

culture.media: Embryonated chicken eggs or cell culture (e.g. MDCK cells) in reference labs
culture.growthCharacteristics: Requires a living host cell; not grown on standard bacteriologic media
culture.colonyMorphology: Not applicable — viruses do not form colonies

identificationClues: Enveloped virion with hemagglutinin (HA) and neuraminidase (NA) surface spikes
Segmented negative-sense ssRNA genome, which allows genetic reassortment (antigenic shift)
Diagnosed clinically and by rapid antigen test or RT-PCR, not by culture in routine practice
Subtyped by HA and NA combinations, e.g. H1N1, H3N2

diseases: Seasonal influenza — fever, myalgia, respiratory symptoms
Pandemic influenza following a major antigenic shift
virulenceFactors: Hemagglutinin — host cell attachment and entry
Neuraminidase — release of new virions from infected cells
High mutation rate and genome segmentation — antigenic drift and shift, enabling immune evasion
clinicalImportance.transmission: Respiratory droplets and contact with contaminated surfaces
clinicalImportance.epidemiology: Causes annual seasonal epidemics and, periodically, global pandemics when a novel HA/NA combination emerges via antigenic shift; vaccine composition is updated yearly to match circulating strains
clinicalImportance.labSignificance: RT-PCR and rapid antigen tests are the primary diagnostic methods used in clinical practice

examFacts.keyBiochemicalReaction: Not applicable — diagnosed by RT-PCR/antigen testing, not biochemical tests
examFacts.distinguishingFeature: Segmented ssRNA genome enabling antigenic shift; HA/NA surface glycoproteins define the subtype
